$comment: The CLOSED set of STATELESS CONTRACT CATALOGUES this repository may publish.
`release-contract.yml` resolves its target here through
`scripts/release_contract.py resolve` and fails closed, so adding a
publishable catalogue is a reviewed diff rather than a dispatch-time
string — the same doctrine as `.github/release-modules.json`,
`.github/release-adapters.json` and `.github/release-connectors.json`.
## Why a FOURTH classification and not a fourth profile
The connector lane deliberately did NOT mint a classification. Its ruling
was that `connector-plugin` would be a synonym: the four properties
`stateless-protocol-adapter` governs — no `ModuleManifest`, no lineage, no
`MIGRATION_OWNER_LEDGER` allocation, no persistence import — are exactly a
connector's four, so a second word would make ADR-0006 and the global
validator describe one thing twice. That ruling stands for connectors.
It does not reach a contract catalogue, because a catalogue differs from an
adapter in a property the four do not cover. An adapter EXISTS to reach a
provider: `dotmac-auth-oidc` ships `transport.py` and declares `httpx` in
`allowed_requires`, and ADR-0006 calls network I/O one of the two concerns
that cannot be faked. A catalogue reaches nothing at all. It is held data —
canonical schema bytes and their digests — and `scripts/release_contract.py`
REFUSES `httpx`, `requests`, `socket`, `urllib` and `subprocess` outright.
So the word buys an enforceable property rather than a synonym: the lane
that permits a network import and the lane that forbids one are not the
same lane, and a package that acquired a provider client would be caught by
its classification rather than only by this file. ADR-0006's 2026-08-26
amendment records the reasoning and supersedes the archived
`release_contract.py` header, which asserted the opposite before the
distinction was identified.
## The classification is checked, not trusted
`resolve` reads the package's `EXTRACTION.toml` and refuses anything whose
`classification` is not `stateless-contract-catalogue`, and refuses an entry
carrying `db_schema`, `manifest_attr`, `integration_floor`, `connector_key`
or `plugin_attr` — a package with those facts belongs in the lane whose
gates will actually ask it questions.
## Why it is empty
ABSENCE IS THE LOCK; the workflow is not. All seven candidate catalogues
(`dotmac-domains-contracts` and the six `dotmac-managed-*-contracts`) exist
only on `archive/worktrees/2026-08-25/starter-managed-services-working` and
declare a `dotmac-kernel` floor of `0.1.0a69` — a number that branch minted
for itself and that mainline later spent on unrelated work. The capability
grammar they import (`CapabilityContractSnapshot`,
`CapabilitySchemaDocument`, `CapabilityCompositionSnapshot`) is on no
published kernel. Until that grammar ships and each catalogue is restacked
onto the release that carries it, this lane resolves nothing and a dispatch
fails at the gate.
Listing a catalogue is one reviewed diff: an entry here, plus the
workflow's `choice` options, which
`tests/architecture/test_contract_release_policy.py` requires to match
exactly once this object is non-empty. Publication is still not adoption —
`EXTRACTION.toml`'s `status` and `contract_consumers` count CONSUMERS, and a
release moves neither.
